title: IGRA as an RD1 blood assay class
dek: Wikipedia's interferon-gamma release assay page names the class. QFT versus T-SPOT and disease-exclusion rules stay on tb-igra-tst.
story: IGRA on Wikipedia (Q6046438) is a class: blood assays that stimulate lymphocytes with Mtb antigens and read IFN-γ. The usual antigens are ESAT-6 and CFP-10 from RD1, which BCG deleted — the point of the class versus PPD.
QuantiFERON (ELISA in tubes) and T-SPOT.TB (ELISPOT) are named instances. This card is the class; those instances get their own glossary plates so the concept map can fork.
The class still does not diagnose disease, grade RIF, or follow treatment. That sentence is repeated because Wikipedia leads sometimes wander into 'diagnosis of TB' language.
deep: Anergy (HIV, steroids, anti-IFN) is a false-negative mechanism, not a lab accident by default.
Grey-zone reproducibility around cut-points is a protocol issue on the clinic plate.
TBST skin tests using similar antigens are cousins, not IGRAs.
Do not order an IGRA to 'check if Ultra was right'.
